This tutorial introduces the statistics behind many human–robot interaction (HRI) studies. Part 1 starts from the basics and builds up one idea at a time, using small made-up studies about how much people trust a robot. Part 2 uses the same tools on a real study. You can run and edit every piece of R code in your browser, with nothing to install.

## Part 1: The basics

| | Chapter | The question it answers |
|---|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Comparing two groups](01-basics.qmd) | Do people trust an expressive robot more than a neutral one? *Mean, variance, the normal distribution, p and alpha, the t-test.* |
| 2 | [Same people, many measurements](02-repeated-measures.qmd) | What goes wrong when each person is measured several times? *Independence, pseudo-replication, the paired t-test.* |
| 3 | [Linear mixed models](03-mixed-models.qmd) | Does trust grow over sessions, and faster with one robot? *Fixed and random effects, random intercepts and slopes, interactions.* |
| 4 | [When the outcome is a rating scale](04-ordinal.qmd) | What if people answer "strongly disagree" to "strongly agree"? *Ordinal regression, odds ratios, ordinal mixed models.* |

Work through the chapters in order. Each one ends with a short exercise and self-check questions.

## Part 2: The Affective Dynamics study

How do trainees feel during robot-mediated human-service training? 66 trainees rehearsed with a robot child that sometimes showed challenging behavior.

| | Page | The question it answers |
|---|------|------------------------|
| 5 | [Design and data](05-study.qmd) | What was measured, and what does the data look like? |
| RQ1 | [Challenging behavior](06-rq1-challenging-behavior.qmd) | How does the recipient's challenging behavior influence trainees' affect? |
| RQ2 | [Own handling](07-rq2-own-handling.qmd) | How do trainees feel about their own handling of that behavior? |
| RQ3 | [After feedback](08-rq3-after-feedback.qmd) | How do trainees feel after receiving feedback from the trainer? |
| RQ4 | [Different functions](09-rq4-functions.qmd) | How does affect differ across challenging behaviors with different functions? |
| | [Model checks](10-model-checks.qmd) | How sure can we be about the answers? |

## The data

**Part 1** uses **simulated** data, so no real participants are involved:

- **Chapter 1:** 40 visitors each meet one robot, neutral or expressive, once, and rate their trust from 0 to 100. [Download](data/robot_one_visit.csv)
- **Chapters 2–4:** 30 people each meet the same robot in 5 weekly sessions. After each session they rate trust from 0 to 100 and answer *"I would trust this robot to help me"* from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). [Download](data/robot_sessions.csv)

The code that creates the data is in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/pourya-shahverdi/hri-stats-tutorial/blob/main/R/simulate_tutorial_data.R).

**Part 2** uses the de-identified study data: 66 trainees × 6 rehearsals × 3 reports = 1,188 rows. [Download](data/affect_n66.csv)

## Using the code boxes

- Code boxes run on their own when the page loads. Press **Run Code** after you edit one, and **Start Over** to bring back the original.
- **Try it** boxes have blanks (`______`) to fill in. Use **Hint** and **Solution** if you get stuck.
- The first page you open downloads R into your browser, which can take a minute. Later pages are faster.
- If code doesn't run, try the [browser check](webr-check.qmd) page or a different browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox work well).
